name: Dwight Freeman
bio: Dwight Freeman was a construction worker and Communist who was among the Hawaii Seven prosecuted under the Smith Act during the McCarthy era. He was convicted in July 1953 of conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government (Smith Act)
sentence: 5 years in prison and a $10,000 fine

charges: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government (Smith Act)
sentence: 5 years in prison and a $10,000 fine

name: Herbert J. Phillips
bio: Herbert J. Phillips was a former University of Washington philosophy professor, fired in 1948, who was jailed for contempt during the Seattle Smith Act trial for refusing to name a fellow Communist as a defense witness. He was prosecuted during the McCarthy era amid the federal campaign against the Communist Party.
charges: Contempt of court (refusal to name a fellow Communist as a defense witness during the Seattle Smith Act trial)
convicted: Jailed for contempt during the trial

bio: Robert A. Campbell was the former Ohio Communist Party educational director, arrested on October 6, 1953, in the Ohio Smith Act roundup during the McCarthy era. He was charged with conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government (Smith Act)

name: Joseph Brandt
bio: Joseph Brandt was the former Ohio Communist Party organizational secretary, arrested on October 6, 1953, in the Ohio Smith Act roundup during the McCarthy era. He was held on $50,000 bail and charged with conspiring to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government.
charges: Conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the U.S. government (Smith Act)

name: Corliss Lamont
bio: Corliss Lamont was an author and civil libertarian indicted for contempt of Congress in 1953 after refusing, on First Amendment grounds, to answer Senator McCarthy's subcommittee. His case became part of the broader First Amendment resistance to congressional investigations during the McCarthy era.
charges: Contempt of Congress

name: Harvey O'Connor
bio: Harvey O'Connor was an author indicted for contempt of Congress in October 1953 for refusing, on First Amendment grounds, to answer Senator McCarthy's questions. His case became part of the broader First Amendment resistance to congressional investigations during the McCarthy era.
charges: Contempt of Congress

name: Barrows Dunham
bio: Barrows Dunham was chairman of Temple University's philosophy department who was suspended and indicted for contempt of Congress after refusing to answer the House Un-American Activities Committee beyond his name and birthdate. His case reflected the McCarthy-era pressure on academics who resisted congressional investigations.
charges: Contempt of Congress

name: Hugh Bryson
bio: Hugh Bryson was president of the Marine Cooks and Stewards union who was indicted in 1953 for perjury on a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit. His prosecution was part of the McCarthy-era campaign against alleged Communist influence in organized labor.
charges: Perjury on a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit

name: Anthony Valentino
bio: Anthony Valentino was a United Electrical Workers figure convicted of falsely signing a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit. His prosecution was part of the McCarthy-era campaign against alleged Communist influence in organized labor.
charges: Falsely signing a Taft-Hartley non-Communist affidavit
sentence: 5 years in prison (on bail pending appeal)

name: Sophie Gerson
bio: Sophie Gerson, wife of New York Communist Party figure Simon Gerson, faced denaturalization and deportation under the Walter-McCarran Act for alleged concealed Communist affiliation. Her case was part of the McCarthy-era use of immigration law against suspected Communists.
charges: Denaturalization/deportation proceedings under the Walter-McCarran Act for alleged concealed Communist affiliation
